questions.q: What do you mainly look for with the gemmological microscope?
questions.why: They tell how the stone formed.

questions.q: At high magnification, what is sharp?
choices: A very thin slice of the stone: you must turn the wheel
questions.why: You go from one slice to another.

questions.q: Fine, parallel needles (the “silk”) rather point to…
Why is a “window” polished on a rough stone?
choices: To see the inside and judge the clarity before cutting

questions.q: Round bubbles in a stone suggest…
choices: a glass or a flame-fusion synthetic
questions.why: It is a clue, to be cross-checked with the other instruments.

questions.q: Which objective gives the highest magnification?
questions.why: The focus must then be very precise.

questions.q: What is the camera of the microscope for?
choices: To photograph what you observe, to attach it to the report
questions.why: The photo is sent to the computer of the laboratory.
